compiled_state.title: As an engineer, the context-augmentation loop is wired into standard, deep, and overlay reviewers with light tier remaining single-shot
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Wire the multi-turn loop (from S3) into the dispatch path for standard, deep (3 specialists + arch synthesis), and overlay reviewers. Light tier remains diff-only single-shot. Update reviewer agent prompts (in plugins/dso/agents/*.md) with a context-request availability section keyed to the documented contract from S1.

**Why**: SC1 extension. Without per-tier wiring, the loop is dead code. Without light-tier opt-out, fast feedback regresses.

**Scope**:
- IN: dispatcher wiring per tier; light-tier opt-out (no augmentation loop); agent prompt updates referencing the contract; tier × loop wiring tests
- OUT: integration tests against live providers (S7); fixture-corpus delta validation (S6)

## Done Definitions

- When complete, standard / deep / overlay reviewers can issue context-requests via the loop and surface grounded findings citing file:line ← Satisfies: SC1 (per-tier wiring)
- When complete, light tier dispatches in single-shot mode with no context-requests in the log ← Satisfies: SC1 (light tier diff-only)
- When complete, agent prompts include a context-request availability section per tier referencing docs/contracts/ci-review-context-request.md ← Satisfies: SC1 (agent awareness)
- When complete, unit tests written and passing assert (a) light-tier dispatch carries no augmentation-loop wiring, (b) standard/deep/overlay tiers do, (c) agent prompts contain the contract reference ← Satisfies: SC6 (tier wiring tests)

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Light-tier opt-OUT is a config refactor risk (4ba1-style) — assert by test that light dispatch has no loop wiring, opt-IN not opt-OUT
- [Reliability] Agent prompt drift from contract version is a real risk — tracked via cross-epic interaction and ref-integrity check follow-up

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
